rows.stem: During adolescence, reproductive phase starts and :

options.label: A
options.text: general growth rate begins to slow down

rows.solution:
At adolescence the reproductive tissues begin to mature, and at the same time the general growth rate of the body begins to slow down. Height and body weight do not decrease, and new hair grows (in the armpits and the genital area, and on the face in boys), so the other choices describe the opposite of what happens.

This is option (A) general growth rate begins to slow down.

rows.stem: Which pair of sex chromosome will determine a male ?
rows.solution:
Women have a perfect pair of sex chromosomes, XX, while men have a mismatched pair, one normal-sized X and a short Y. So the pair XY determines a male.

This is option (C) XY.

rows.stem: One of the events that does not occur during photosynthesis is :

options.label: B
options.text: Carbon dioxide is released during the process.

options.label: C
options.text: Oxygen is released during the process.

options.label: D
options.text: Carbon dioxide is absorbed during the process.

rows.solution:
In photosynthesis, chlorophyll absorbs light energy, carbon dioxide is taken in and reduced to carbohydrate, and oxygen is released:

\(\mathrm{6CO_2 + 12H_2O \xrightarrow[\text{chlorophyll}]{\text{sunlight}} C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 + 6H_2O}\)

Carbon dioxide is absorbed, not released, so the event that does not occur is option (B) Carbon dioxide is released during the process.

rows.stem: Two LED bulbs of 10W and 5W are connected in series. If the current flowing through 5W bulb is 0.005A, the current flowing through 10W bulb is :
rows.solution:
In a series combination the same current flows through every element, whatever its power rating. So the current through the 10 W bulb is also 0.005 A.

This is option (C) 0.005A.

rows.stem:
(i) State the essential function performed by ozone at the higher levels of the atmosphere.

(ii) Why was there a sharp drop in the amount of ozone in the atmosphere in 1980’s.
rows.solution:
(i) The ozone layer at the higher levels of the atmosphere shields the surface of the earth from the harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation of the Sun.

(ii) The sharp drop was caused by synthetic chemicals, the chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), which were widely used as refrigerants, in fire extinguishers and in aerosol sprays. They reach the upper atmosphere and break down the ozone.

rows.stem: Give two reasons, why bile juice is considered to be an important secretion of liver in the process of digestion ?
rows.solution:
Two reasons (bile is made in the liver and stored in the gall bladder):

1. The food coming from the stomach is acidic. Bile juice makes it alkaline, so that the pancreatic enzymes can act on it.

2. The bile salts break the large globules of fat into smaller globules (emulsification of fat). This increases the surface area for the fat-digesting enzymes (lipase) to act on.

rows.stem: Name the hormone secreted in scary situations by animals. Write any three responses which enable the animal body to deal with it.
rows.solution:
The hormone is adrenaline, secreted by the adrenal glands directly into the blood.

Any three responses:

1. The heart beats faster, so more oxygen is supplied to the muscles.

2. The blood supply to the digestive system is reduced, because the small arteries around it contract.

3. The blood supply to the skin is reduced, so that more blood is diverted to the skeletal muscles.

4. The breathing rate increases, because the diaphragm and the rib muscles contract more.

Together these prepare the body to deal with the situation (to fight or to run).

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: List two differences in the characteristic properties of the virtual images formed by the two types of spherical lenses (concave and convex). How are these characteristics of the two lenses used in the correction of the two common defects of vision namely myopia and hypermetropia ?
rows.solution:
Two differences between the virtual images formed by the two lenses:

1. The virtual image formed by a concave lens is always diminished (magnification less than 1), while the virtual image formed by a convex lens is magnified (magnification more than 1).

2. For a concave lens the image is nearer the lens than the object (image distance less than object distance), while for a convex lens the virtual image is farther from the lens than the object (image distance more than object distance).

Use in correcting the defects of vision:

Myopia (short-sightedness): the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens of suitable power is used. It forms a virtual image of the distant object nearer the eye, at the far point of the myopic eye, so the eye lens brings the image back onto the retina.

Hypermetropia (far-sightedness): the image of a nearby object forms behind the retina. A convex (converging) lens of suitable power is used. It forms a virtual image of the nearby object farther away, at the near point of the hypermetropic eye, so the eye lens brings the image back onto the retina.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem:
An object is kept at a distance of 1m from a lens of power +2D :

(i) Identify the type of lens.

(ii) Calculate its focal length and distance of the image formed.
rows.solution:
(i) The power is positive, so the lens is a convex (converging) lens.

(ii) \(f = \dfrac{1}{P} = \dfrac{1}{2}\) m \(= 0.5\) m \(= 50\) cm.

With \(u = -100\) cm, the lens formula \(\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\) gives

\(\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{50} - \dfrac{1}{100} = \dfrac{1}{100}\), so \(v = +100\) cm \(= 1\) m.

The image forms 1 m from the lens on the other side. This also follows without the formula: the object is at \(2F_1\) (\(u = 2f = 100\) cm), so the image is at \(2F_2\), real, inverted and of the same size.

rows.stem:
Define the following terms in the context of a diverging lens :

(i) Principal focus,

(ii) Focal length.

Draw a labelled ray diagram to illustrate your answer.
rows.solution:
A diverging lens is a concave lens.

(i) Principal focus: the point on the principal axis from which rays of light parallel to the principal axis appear to diverge after refraction through the lens. It lies on the same side as the incident light.

(ii) Focal length: the distance between the optical centre and the principal focus of the lens.

Ray diagram: draw a concave lens with its principal axis and optical centre O. Draw a few rays parallel to the principal axis falling on the lens from the left, and show them bending away from the axis after refraction (diverging). Produce the refracted rays backward with dotted lines; they meet on the axis at the principal focus F, on the left of the lens. Mark the distance OF as the focal length, and put arrows on the rays.

rows.subtopic: Chemical Properties of Acids and Bases
rows.stem:
(i) Why is acidified water considered to be a good conductor of electricity ?

(ii) Write a chemical equation showing the ionic products formed on dissolving potassium hydroxide in water.

(iii) Care must be taken while diluting concentrated nitric acid with water. Why ?
rows.solution:
(i) Acidified water contains more ions than pure water: the acid gives hydrogen ions (\(\mathrm{H^+}\), as \(\mathrm{H_3O^+}\)) and its negative ions in solution. These ions carry the current, so acidified water conducts electricity well.

(ii) Potassium hydroxide dissolves in water and gives potassium ions and hydroxide ions:

\(\mathrm{KOH(s) \xrightarrow{H_2O} K^+(aq) + OH^-(aq)}\)

(iii) Mixing concentrated nitric acid with water is a highly exothermic process. If water is added to the concentrated acid, the heat released can make the mixture splash out and cause burns, or crack the container because of excessive local heating. So the acid must be added slowly to water, with constant stirring.

rows.stem:
(i) It is observed that covalent compounds are bad conductors of electricity. Give reason.

(ii) Carbon can neither form \(\mathrm{C^{4+}}\) cation nor \(\mathrm{C^{4-}}\) anion. Why ?

(iii) Draw electron dot structure of Ethanol.

(iv) Identify hetero atom(s) in the following compounds :

(a) \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COCH_3}\)

(b) \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl}\)
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - part (iv)(a) prints butanone as a condensed structure, CH3CH2 - C - CH3 with the double-bonded O drawn vertically under the middle carbon; typed losslessly here as the condensed formula, so the row is answerable from text, but the drawing is the printed form. Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
(i) Covalent compounds are made of molecules held by shared electron pairs. They do not form ions, so they have no free ions (or free electrons) to carry a current. That is why they are bad conductors of electricity.

(ii) Carbon has four valence electrons (2, 4).

It does not form the \(\mathrm{C^{4+}}\) cation, because removing four electrons would need a very large amount of energy.

It does not form the \(\mathrm{C^{4-}}\) anion, because a nucleus with six protons could not hold on to ten electrons, given the small size of the atom.

So carbon shares its electrons and forms covalent bonds.

(iii) Ethanol is \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}OH}\). In its electron dot structure, the first carbon shares one pair of electrons with each of three hydrogen atoms and one pair with the second carbon. The second carbon shares one pair with each of two hydrogen atoms, one pair with the first carbon and one pair with the oxygen atom. The oxygen shares one pair with the second carbon and one pair with a hydrogen atom, and keeps two lone pairs of its own. Each shared pair is drawn as one dot and one cross between the two atoms, so every carbon and the oxygen has eight electrons around it and every hydrogen has two.

(iv) An atom other than carbon and hydrogen in a carbon compound is a hetero atom.

(a) In \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COCH_3}\) (butanone) the hetero atom is oxygen.

(b) In \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl}\) (chloroethane) the hetero atom is chlorine.

rows.stem:
(i) What are soaps ? Explain the mechanism of cleansing action of soap with the help of a labelled diagram.

(ii) Detergents are better than soaps. Justify.
rows.solution:
(i) Soaps are the sodium or potassium salts of long-chain carboxylic acids, for example \(\mathrm{RCOO^-Na^+}\).

A soap molecule has two ends: an ionic end, which is hydrophilic (dissolves in water), and a long hydrocarbon chain, which is hydrophobic (dissolves in oil). Most dirt is oily and does not dissolve in water. When soap is added to water, the molecules arrange themselves in clusters called micelles: the hydrocarbon tails point inwards into the oily dirt, while the ionic ends face outwards into the water. The oily dirt is collected in the centre of the micelle, which forms an emulsion in water. The micelles stay in solution and do not come together, because the ionic ends on their surfaces repel one another. So the dirt suspended in the micelles is easily rinsed away, and the clothes are cleaned.

Diagram: draw a circle of soap molecules round an oil droplet at the centre. Each molecule is drawn as a zig-zag line (the hydrocarbon tail) with a small circle at its outer end (the ionic end, \(\mathrm{COO^-}\)), and \(\mathrm{Na^+}\) ions near the outer ends. Label the oil droplet, the hydrocarbon tail, the ionic end and the micelle.

(ii) Detergents are better cleansing agents than soaps because they do not form insoluble precipitates (scum) with the calcium and magnesium ions present in hard water. So they work well in hard water too, while soap is wasted forming scum and cleans poorly.
